project_description: A web-based application designed to streamline and automate the process of employees applying for leave and managers reviewing and approving these requests. It replaces manual leave tracking with a centralized digital solution to improve efficiency, accuracy, and record-keeping across the organization.

executive_summary.project_overview: The Employee Leave Management System (ELMS) is a strategic initiative to modernize internal HR processes. This web-based application will provide a centralized digital platform for employees to submit leave requests, view balances and history, and for managers to efficiently review, approve, or reject these requests. The system aims to eliminate manual paperwork and enhance the overall efficiency of leave administration across the organization.
executive_summary.business_problem: Current manual leave tracking processes lead to inefficiencies, potential errors in balance management, delays in request approvals, and excessive paperwork. This results in significant administrative burden for HR, managers, and employees, hindering productivity and accurate record-keeping across the enterprise.
executive_summary.business_need: There is a critical need for a streamlined, centralized, and secure digital solution to manage employee leave. This includes simplifying the leave application process, accurately maintaining leave balances, enabling timely manager approvals, providing comprehensive leave history, and significantly reducing reliance on manual paperwork to enhance operational efficiency and compliance.
executive_summary.proposed_solution: Implement a secure, web-based Employee Leave Management System with distinct modules for employees, managers, and HR administrators. This system will facilitate online leave applications, real-time balance tracking, a structured approval workflow for managers, and robust administrative capabilities for HR, all accessible through a responsive user interface with role-based access control.
business_benefits: Simplified and intuitive leave application process for all employees.
Automated and accurate maintenance of employee leave balances.
Expedited review and approval workflow for managers, reducing delays.
Centralized access to comprehensive leave history for employees and managers.
Significant reduction in manual paperwork and associated administrative overhead.
Improved data accuracy and compliance in leave management processes.
Enhanced transparency and visibility into organizational leave patterns for HR.
executive_summary.expected_outcome: A fully functional, user-friendly Employee Leave Management System that significantly reduces administrative effort, improves the accuracy of leave records, and enhances the overall efficiency and transparency of the leave management process for all employees, managers, and HR administrators. The system will provide real-time insights into leave utilization and outstanding requests, supporting better workforce planning.

epics.title: Employee Self-Service Leave Management
epics.business_objective: Empower employees with a user-friendly digital platform to independently manage their leave requests, view their leave entitlements, and track their leave history, thereby reducing administrative reliance and improving employee satisfaction.
epics.business_value: Increased employee satisfaction and autonomy through self-service capabilities, improved transparency regarding leave entitlements and usage, and reduced administrative burden on HR and managers by automating common employee inquiries and tasks related to leave.
epics.detailed_description: This epic focuses on developing all functionalities accessible to employees. It includes features for employees to securely log in, view their current leave balances across various types, submit new leave requests specifying type, dates, and reason, and monitor the status of their pending requests. Employees will also be able to cancel pending requests and access their comprehensive historical leave records.
scope: Viewing available leave balances for different leave types (e.g., Annual, Sick, Personal).
Applying for various types of leave via an online form.
Specifying start and end dates for leave requests, including partial days.
Providing a mandatory reason for leave submission.
Viewing the real-time status of submitted leave requests (Pending, Approved, Rejected).
Cancelling pending leave requests before manager action.
Accessing a comprehensive personal leave history with details of past leaves.
out_of_scope: Direct integration with external payroll systems for automated leave accrual calculations beyond basic annual reset.
Complex leave policy rules implementation (e.g., FMLA, parental leave specific regional compliance rules).
Multi-level approval workflows for managers (e.g., manager approval then HR approval).
Automated email notifications for all leave status changes (initially, manual notifications only).
Mobile application for leave management (web-based only).
assumptions: Employees will have unique login credentials managed by the HR system.
Each employee is assigned to one direct reporting manager for leave approval purposes.
Leave balances are reset annually according to predefined organizational policies configured by HR.
Initial leave balances will be manually imported or set by HR administrators at system go-live.
All required leave types and their basic rules (e.g., maximum days) are pre-defined by HR.
dependencies: A functioning user authentication service must be available.
Core HR employee data (names, employee IDs, reporting manager, department) must be accessible.
Defined leave types and initial balances, as configured by HR, must be present in the system.
risks: Low user adoption due to a cumbersome or non-intuitive user experience (UX) if not designed carefully.
Security vulnerabilities if authentication and authorization mechanisms are not robustly implemented, leading to unauthorized access.
Data integrity issues if leave balances are not updated correctly after approvals, causing employee dissatisfaction.
Compliance risks if organizational leave policies are not accurately reflected and enforced by the system.
success_metrics: 90% of employees successfully submitting leave requests via the system within 3 months post-launch.
Average time taken for an employee to apply for leave reduced by 50% compared to manual process.
Reduction in employee inquiries to HR regarding leave balances by 40%.
Achieve a system uptime of 99.9% for the employee module during business hours.

features.title: Employee Leave Application & Submission
features.description: Enables employees to initiate and submit new leave requests through a digital interface, allowing them to select appropriate leave types, specify desired dates, and provide a mandatory reason, thereby streamlining the application process.
functional_requirements: Employee shall be able to log in securely using their credentials.
Employee shall be able to navigate to a dedicated 'Apply for Leave' section.
Employee shall be able to select a leave type from a predefined list (e.g., Annual, Sick, Unpaid).
Employee shall be able to enter a start date and an end date for the leave request.
Employee shall be able to provide a mandatory reason for the leave in a text field.
Employee shall be able to review and submit the completed leave request form.
Employee shall be able to cancel any pending leave requests that have not yet been acted upon by their manager.
non_functional_requirements: Response time for submitting a leave request shall be below 2 seconds.
Secure data transmission (HTTPS) for all leave request details to protect sensitive employee information.
The user interface for the application form must be intuitive and responsive across standard browsers.
System shall provide clear visual feedback upon successful submission or any validation errors.
technical_notes: Requires a RESTful API endpoint (/api/leave/submit) for handling leave request submissions.
Frontend implementation using a modern JavaScript framework (e.g., React, Angular) with form validation logic.
Integration with the authentication service to verify employee identity and permissions.
Database schema adjustments to store leave requests including type, dates, reason, status, and employee ID.
dependencies: Active user authentication service for employee login.
Predefined list of configurable leave types from HR module.
Employee profile data including their reporting manager.
acceptance_criteria: Given a logged-in employee navigates to the 'Apply Leave' section, When they fill in all mandatory fields (Leave Type, Start Date, End Date, Reason) and click 'Submit', Then the request is successfully submitted, and a confirmation message is displayed.
Given an employee has a pending leave request, When they select it and click 'Cancel Request', Then the request status changes to 'Cancelled', and they are notified.
When an employee attempts to submit a leave request with a start date in the past, Then an error message 'Leave start date cannot be in the past' is displayed, and the request is not submitted.
When an employee submits a request, Then their manager is notified of the new pending request.

stories.title: Submit New Leave Request
stories.detailed_description: As an employee, I need a clear and intuitive way to submit a new leave request, including selecting the leave type, specifying the start and end dates, and providing a comprehensive reason, so that my request can be processed efficiently by my manager and my leave is officially recorded.
business_rules: Leave start date must be a future date or today's date.
Leave end date must be on or after the leave start date.
A specific leave type must be selected from the predefined list.
A reason for leave must be provided, with a minimum length of 10 characters.
The system must prevent submission of overlapping leave requests for the same employee.
Minimum leave duration allowed is 0.5 days (half-day leave).
stories.i_want: to apply for a new leave request online
stories.so_that: my manager can review and approve it, and my leave is officially recorded without manual paperwork.
preconditions: Employee is logged into the Employee Leave Management System.
Employee has an active employment status in the system.
Employee has access to the 'Apply for Leave' functionality.
postconditions: A new leave request entry is created in the database with a 'Pending' status.
The employee's direct manager is notified of the new pending leave request.
The employee can view the newly submitted request in their 'Pending Requests' list.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as an employee, When I navigate to the 'Apply Leave' section, Then I should see a form with fields for Leave Type, Start Date, End Date, and Reason.
When I successfully fill in all mandatory fields and click 'Submit', Then a confirmation message is displayed, and the request status is 'Pending' in my history.
When I attempt to submit a leave request with a start date prior to today's date, Then an error message 'Leave start date cannot be in the past' is displayed.
When I try to submit a request without providing a reason, Then an error message 'Leave reason is mandatory' is displayed.
When I successfully submit a leave request, Then my manager receives an alert or notification about the new request.

tasks.title: Implement Leave Request Submission API and UI
tasks.description: Develop the frontend user interface for the leave application form, including date pickers, leave type dropdown, and reason text area with client-side validation. Create the backend API endpoint to receive and validate leave request data, persist it to the database with 'Pending' status, and integrate a basic manager notification mechanism.
tasks.definition_of_done: Frontend leave application form is fully functional, responsive, and includes client-side validation. Backend API endpoint is developed, secured, validated, and capable of storing leave requests in the database. Unit and integration tests for both frontend and backend are passed. Basic manager notification is triggered upon successful submission. Code reviewed and deployed to development environment.

features.title: Employee Leave Balance & History View
features.description: Provides employees with a clear and concise overview of their current leave balances for different leave types and a comprehensive historical record of all their past, present, and pending leave requests.
functional_requirements: Employee shall be able to view their available leave balance for each specific leave type (e.g., Annual, Sick, Personal).
Employee shall be able to view a chronological list of all past approved and rejected leave requests.
Employee shall be able to view a list of all currently pending leave requests.
Employee shall be able to view detailed information for each individual leave request (including type, start/end dates, reason, status, and any manager comments).
The system shall accurately calculate and display remaining leave balances in real-time based on approved and consumed leave.
non_functional_requirements: Response time for loading leave balances and history shall be below 1 second.
The data displayed for leave balances and history must be 100% accurate and up-to-date.
The interface for viewing leave details should be easily navigable, readable, and provide filtering/sorting options.
Data displayed must respect employee-level privacy and only show personal leave information.
technical_notes: Requires API endpoints to fetch current leave balances from the database and historical leave request data.
Frontend component to render a summary dashboard for balances and a detailed table/list for history.
Backend logic for calculating remaining leave balances, considering accruals and approved leaves.
Implementation of pagination and filtering for large historical leave datasets.
dependencies: Accurate leave balance calculation logic within the backend.
Reliable storage and retrieval of all leave request data.
acceptance_criteria: A logged-in employee can view an accurate summary of their total available leave balance for each leave type on their dashboard.
Employee can access a list of all their submitted leave requests, clearly showing type, dates, reason, and current status (Pending, Approved, Rejected).
Employee can click on any specific leave request entry to view its comprehensive detailed information.
Leave balances are dynamically updated and accurately reflected immediately after a leave request is approved or rejected.

stories.title: View Personal Leave Details
stories.detailed_description: As an employee, I want to clearly see my current leave balances for all applicable leave types and a comprehensive history of my past and pending leave requests, including their current statuses and any associated comments, so that I can keep track of my entitlements and past usage without needing to contact HR or my manager.
business_rules: Leave balances displayed must reflect only approved and consumed leave, not pending requests.
Pending requests should be clearly marked and listed separately from approved/rejected history.
Leave history should be viewable by calendar year and filterable by leave status (e.g., Approved, Rejected, Pending).
All date calculations (e.g., total days taken) must be precise.
Rejected requests must display the manager's comments.
stories.i_want: to view my up-to-date leave balances and a complete history of my leave requests
stories.so_that: I am fully aware of my remaining leave days and can track my past leave usage and future plans effectively.
preconditions: Employee is logged into the system.
Employee has existing leave balances (even if zero) or historical leave requests.
The system has processed at least one leave request for the employee.
postconditions: Employee successfully views their current leave balance summary on their dashboard.
Employee successfully views a detailed, filterable list of their leave request history.
Employee has clear visibility into the status and details of each leave request.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as an employee, When I navigate to my 'Leave Dashboard', Then I should see an accurate summary of my current available leave balances by type.
When I navigate to the 'Leave History' section, Then I should see a list of all my leave requests, including Type, Start Date, End Date, Reason, and Status.
When a new leave is approved, Then my leave balance displayed on the dashboard is updated accordingly in real-time.
When I view a rejected request, Then any comments provided by the manager during rejection are clearly visible.
When I filter my leave history by 'Approved' status, Then only approved requests are displayed.

tasks.title: Develop Employee Leave Dashboard
tasks.description: Implement the frontend dashboard component that clearly displays current leave balances for all types. Develop the leave history table component that integrates with backend APIs to fetch and display historical leave data, including status and manager comments. Ensure the history table includes basic filtering by status and chronological sorting capabilities.
tasks.definition_of_done: Frontend dashboard for leave balances is fully implemented and displays accurate data. Leave history table component is developed, populated with mock data, and integrated with the backend API to fetch real data. Filtering and sorting functionality for leave history is operational. Unit tests for UI components and data display logic are passed. Code reviewed and deployed to development environment.

epics.title: Administrative Leave Management & Policy Control
epics.business_objective: Provide managers and HR administrators with robust tools to efficiently manage employee leave requests, enforce organizational leave policies, maintain accurate employee records, and generate critical leave-related reports, enhancing operational control.
epics.business_value: Streamlined and expedited approval workflows for managers, enhanced compliance with organizational leave policies, significant reduction in administrative overhead for HR and managers, improved data accuracy for strategic reporting, and better data-driven insights into organizational leave patterns.
epics.detailed_description: This epic encompasses all functionalities required by managers and HR administrators. For managers, it enables reviewing, approving, or rejecting pending employee leave requests, with the ability to add mandatory comments for rejections. For HR administrators, it provides comprehensive capabilities for creating and managing employee accounts, configuring and updating organizational leave policies, adjusting individual employee leave balances, and generating organization-wide leave reports for strategic oversight.
scope: Secure login for managers and HR administrators with appropriate role-based access.
Managers viewing a filtered list of pending leave requests specifically from their direct reports.
Managers approving submitted leave requests with a single action.
Managers rejecting submitted leave requests, requiring mandatory comments for rationale.
Managers viewing the complete leave history of their direct reports.
HR administrators creating new employee accounts with essential details (e.g., name, department, reporting manager).
HR administrators modifying global organizational leave policies (e.g., adding new leave types, adjusting annual accrual rates).
HR administrators updating individual employee leave balances with an audit trail.
HR administrators viewing and generating comprehensive organization-wide leave reports (e.g., leave utilization by department, total pending requests).
out_of_scope: Automated complex leave accrual calculations based on dynamic rules (e.g., tenure-based accrual, specific union agreements).
Direct integration with payroll systems for automated leave payout calculations or complex financial adjustments.
Advanced analytics, forecasting, or predictive modeling capabilities for future leave patterns.
Detailed, granular audit trails for every single policy change (beyond high-level logging).
Workflow delegation functionality for managers (e.g., assigning approval duties to another manager temporarily).
assumptions: Managers will have a clearly defined reporting structure in the system to identify their direct reports.
HR administrators will have elevated and distinct permissions to perform system-wide configurations and data modifications.
Predefined initial leave types and policies will be established and available for configuration by HR.
Access to the HR module will be strictly restricted to designated HR personnel through robust access controls.
dependencies: Accurate and up-to-date employee data, including reporting lines and department assignments.
Well-defined and documented organizational leave policies.
A robust role-based access control (RBAC) mechanism for securing administrative functions.
The employee self-service module must be functional to generate requests for managers to review.
risks: Security breach if RBAC is not implemented correctly or if administrative credentials are compromised.
Managerial resistance if the approval process is overly cumbersome or lacks necessary information.
Policy misconfiguration by HR leading to incorrect leave calculations or non-compliance issues.
Data privacy concerns arising from HR access to sensitive employee leave and personal data if not properly secured.
Performance degradation during report generation for large datasets if not optimized.
success_metrics: 95% of manager leave approvals/rejections completed within 24 business hours of submission.
Reduction in HR manual efforts for individual leave balance adjustments by 70%.
Accuracy of all organization-wide leave reports consistently maintained at 100%.
Zero unauthorized access attempts to the HR module within 6 months post-system launch.
Managers report a 'Good' or 'Excellent' satisfaction level with the approval workflow.

features.title: Managerial Leave Request Review & Approval
features.description: Provides managers with a dedicated interface to view, evaluate, and act upon pending leave requests submitted by their direct reports, allowing them to efficiently approve or reject requests and provide necessary feedback.
functional_requirements: Manager shall be able to log in securely using their credentials.
Manager shall be able to view a dashboard presenting a filtered list of all pending leave requests from their direct reports.
Manager shall be able to view detailed information for each pending leave request.
Manager shall be able to approve a pending leave request, changing its status to 'Approved'.
Manager shall be able to reject a pending leave request, changing its status to 'Rejected'.
Manager shall be required to add mandatory comments when rejecting a leave request, providing a clear rationale.
Manager shall be able to view the complete leave history of any of their direct reports.
non_functional_requirements: Secure authentication and authorization (RBAC) specifically for managers.
Response time for loading the pending requests list shall be below 2 seconds.
The user interface for approval/rejection actions must be clear, unambiguous, and efficient.
Data integrity must be maintained for all status updates and balance adjustments post-approval/rejection.
technical_notes: Requires a RESTful API endpoint (/api/manager/requests) to fetch pending requests for a specific manager's reports.
API endpoints (/api/leave/{id}/approve, /api/leave/{id}/reject) for updating request status and adding comments.
Database transactions to ensure atomic updates for leave request status and employee leave balances.
Frontend component for the manager dashboard, including request details and action buttons.
dependencies: Accurate and up-to-date employee-manager reporting structure data.
Existing leave request data from the employee module.
User authentication service with role-based access for managers.
acceptance_criteria: A logged-in manager can view all pending leave requests submitted by their direct reports on a dedicated dashboard.
Manager can successfully approve a pending leave request, changing its status to 'Approved' and updating the employee's balance.
Manager can successfully reject a pending leave request, changing its status to 'Rejected' and recording the provided mandatory comments.
The employee who submitted the request is automatically notified of the manager's decision (approval or rejection).
Manager can access and view the full leave history of any employee who directly reports to them.

stories.title: Process Employee Leave Requests
stories.detailed_description: As a manager, I need to easily view pending leave requests from my direct reports and have clear options to approve or reject them, with the ability to add mandatory comments for rejections, so that I can efficiently manage my team's availability, ensure timely processing of leave, and provide clear communication to my employees.
business_rules: Only the direct reporting manager can approve or reject their employees' leave requests.
Rejection of a leave request requires a mandatory comment from the manager, with a minimum length of 15 characters.
Approving a request must automatically debit the corresponding leave balance from the employee's available days.
Once a request is approved or rejected, its status cannot be changed by the manager through the same interface.
Managers can only view leave requests and history for their direct reports.
stories.i_want: to review and act on my employees' leave requests promptly and clearly
stories.so_that: I can manage team availability effectively and ensure fair and timely processing of leave requests.
preconditions: Manager is logged into the Employee Leave Management System.
There are pending leave requests from the manager's direct reports.
Manager has the appropriate 'Manager' role permissions assigned.
postconditions: The status of the leave request is updated to either 'Approved' or 'Rejected' in the system.
The employee who submitted the request is notified of the manager's decision.
If rejected, the manager's comments are permanently recorded with the request.
If approved, the employee's available leave balance for the specific type is accurately debited.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as a manager, When I access my dashboard, Then I see a distinct list of pending leave requests from only my direct reports.
When I click 'Approve' on a request, Then its status changes to 'Approved', and the employee's corresponding leave balance is accurately debited.
When I click 'Reject' on a request without providing any comments, Then an error message 'Comments are mandatory for rejection' is displayed, and the rejection is not processed.
When I click 'Reject' on a request and provide comments, Then its status changes to 'Rejected', and the comments are saved with the request.
When I view a direct report's leave history, Then I can see all their past approved, rejected, and pending requests with full details.

tasks.title: Create Manager Leave Request Workflow
tasks.description: Develop the backend logic and API endpoints for managers to fetch pending leave requests specifically for their direct reports, and to update the status of a request to 'Approved' or 'Rejected'. Implement the mandatory comments feature for rejections and ensure correct leave balance adjustments upon approval. Design and implement the manager's dashboard UI component to display these requests and facilitate actions.
tasks.definition_of_done: Backend API for manager approvals/rejections is fully developed, secured, and unit-tested. Frontend manager dashboard for displaying pending requests and taking action is implemented and validated. Mandatory comments for rejection are enforced by the backend. Leave balance update logic upon approval is implemented and tested for accuracy. Integration tests covering the entire manager workflow pass successfully. Code reviewed and deployed to development environment.

features.title: HR Leave Policy & Employee Account Management
features.description: Empowers HR administrators with a comprehensive set of tools to manage organizational leave policies, create and update employee accounts, modify individual employee leave balances, and generate essential reports for strategic oversight and compliance.
functional_requirements: HR administrator shall be able to create new employee accounts, including basic profile information and initial reporting structure.
HR administrator shall be able to modify existing employee account details (e.g., department, reporting manager, employment status).
HR administrator shall be able to define and modify global leave policies (e.g., add new leave types, adjust default annual accrual rates, define maximum carry-over).
HR administrator shall be able to manually update individual employee leave balances with a mandatory reason for adjustment.
HR administrator shall be able to view and generate organization-wide leave reports (e.g., total leave utilization by department, list of all pending requests, upcoming leaves).
All HR actions related to policy and balance changes shall be logged for auditing purposes.
non_functional_requirements: Secure authentication and robust authorization (highest level of RBAC) for HR module access is critical.
Data integrity for policy and employee account changes is paramount to prevent inconsistencies.
System response time for administrative tasks (e.g., creating accounts, updating policies) should be efficient (under 3 seconds).
A comprehensive audit trail for all HR-initiated changes to policies and balances must be maintained.
The HR interface must be intuitive and minimize risk of errors in critical data entry.
technical_notes: Requires robust RBAC implementation to ensure only authorized HR personnel can access and modify settings.
Dedicated API endpoints for managing employee data, leave types, and global leave policies.
Database schema extensions for storing configurable leave policies and detailed employee attributes.
Integration with a reporting engine or custom query builder for generating dynamic organization-wide reports.
dependencies: Core user authentication and authorization service with robust role management.
A centralized employee data store for profile management.
Reporting framework or library for data aggregation and visualization.
acceptance_criteria: A logged-in HR administrator can successfully create a new employee account with all required details and assign a reporting manager.
HR can modify an existing employee's department or reporting manager and save the changes.
HR can define a new leave type, specify its default annual balance, and enable/disable it for use by employees.
HR can manually adjust an individual employee's leave balance for any leave type, with a mandatory reason for the adjustment.
HR can generate a report showing total approved leave days across all departments for a specified date range.
All modifications made by HR administrators are recorded in an audit log, detailing who made the change and when.

stories.title: Manage Organizational Leave Settings
stories.detailed_description: As an HR administrator, I need a comprehensive and secure interface to manage employee accounts, define and update global leave policies, accurately adjust individual employee leave balances, and generate organization-wide reports, so that I can maintain accurate records, ensure consistent policy compliance, and gain valuable insights into organizational leave patterns for workforce planning.
business_rules: Only users explicitly assigned the 'HR Administrator' role can access the HR module functionalities.
Creating a new employee account requires unique employee ID, full name, department, and assignment of a reporting manager.
Modifying global leave policies requires confirmation and clear communication of the impact on future leave accruals and applications.
Updating an individual's leave balance requires a mandatory reason/comment explaining the adjustment for auditing purposes.
All generated reports must be based on real-time system data and reflect current statuses and balances.
Any changes to employee profiles or leave policies must trigger an audit log entry.
stories.i_want: to manage employee accounts, configure leave policies, and generate comprehensive reports
stories.so_that: I can ensure the system accurately reflects current organizational rules, maintain precise employee records, and provide data-driven insights for HR operations and compliance.
preconditions: HR administrator is logged into the system with appropriate 'HR Administrator' permissions.
The system has existing employee data and defined leave policies (even default ones).
postconditions: Employee accounts are accurately created, modified, or deactivated as per HR actions.
Global leave policies are correctly configured and applied across the organization.
Individual employee leave balances are adjusted with clear justification and an audit trail.
Relevant organization-wide reports are generated based on specified criteria, providing accurate data.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as an HR administrator, When I navigate to the 'Employee Management' section, Then I can successfully create a new employee account with all mandatory fields and assign a reporting manager.
When I navigate to the 'Leave Policy Configuration' section, Then I can add a new custom leave type with its default annual balance and save it.
When I select an employee and go to 'Manage Balances', Then I can manually adjust their balance for a specific leave type, providing a mandatory reason for the adjustment.
When I generate an 'Organization-wide Leave Utilization Report' for a specific quarter, Then it shows accurate aggregated data on leave consumption by department.
When I modify an employee's reporting manager, Then the change is saved, and an audit log entry is created detailing the action.

tasks.title: Build HR Administration Interface
tasks.description: Develop the HR administration UI for creating/modifying employee accounts, configuring leave types and policies, and manually adjusting leave balances. Implement backend APIs to support these operations, ensuring robust data validation, comprehensive auditing, and strict role-based access control. Design the necessary database schema changes for policy management and enhanced employee attributes.
tasks.definition_of_done: Full HR module UI for employee management, policy configuration, and balance adjustment is implemented, tested for usability. All backend APIs for HR functions are developed, unit-tested, and integration-tested. Robust role-based access control is strictly enforced for all HR module access points. Database schema supports new HR functionalities including audit logging for critical actions. Code reviewed and deployed to UAT environment.

non_functional_requirements.performance: The system shall exhibit a response time below 2 seconds for all critical user interactions (e.g., login, submitting leave requests, viewing personal leave history, manager approvals). The application must be capable of supporting 500 concurrent users without any noticeable degradation in response time or system stability. All organizational reports, even for large datasets, shall be generated and displayed within 10 seconds.
non_functional_requirements.security: Implement secure authentication for all user roles using industry best practices including password hashing (e.g., BCrypt), salting, and multi-factor authentication (MFA) capabilities. Enforce robust role-based access control (RBAC) to ensure users can only access functionalities and data explicitly authorized for their role. All data, both at rest and in transit, must be encrypted (TLS 1.2+ for transit, AES-256 for at rest). Regular security audits, penetration testing, and vulnerability scanning must be performed. The system shall adhere to OWASP Top 10 security guidelines.
non_functional_requirements.availability: The Employee Leave Management System shall maintain a high availability target of 99.9% uptime during standard business hours (Monday-Friday, 8 AM - 6 PM local time). Daily automated database backups must be performed with a minimum 7-day retention policy. A comprehensive disaster recovery plan will be in place, targeting a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of 4 hours and a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 24 hours. Critical infrastructure components will be designed for redundancy and failover.
non_functional_requirements.scalability: The system architecture must be designed to support future growth, allowing for an increase of up to 50% in the number of employees and concurrent users over the next 2 years without requiring significant re-architecture or causing performance degradation. The application should support horizontal scaling of web servers and application servers. The database should be capable of accommodating read replicas or sharding for high read/write loads if required in the future.
non_functional_requirements.reliability: All critical transactions within the system, such as leave submission, approval, rejection, and leave balance updates, must be atomic, consistent, isolated, and durable (ACID compliant). The system will incorporate comprehensive error logging and monitoring solutions (e.g., ELK stack, Prometheus) for immediate detection and alerting of issues. Automated data validation mechanisms will be in place at both frontend and backend to prevent inconsistent data states. The user interface shall provide graceful error handling and informative, user-friendly messages for any system failures or validation issues.
